issues.description: Error message types raise APIConnectionError mid-loop, leaking through recv_task's exception handler instead of terminating cleanly
issues.detail: In _process_stream_event, server-side errors (auth_error, quota_exceeded, etc.) raise APIConnectionError, but recv_task wraps the call in a broad try/except that logs and continues. The error gets swallowed by the same except Exception that handles JSON parse failures. Separate the data path (transcripts) from the control path (errors): return a typed event or set a failure flag, and let _run handle reconnect or shutdown.

issues.description: audio_format field on STTOptions duplicates sample_rate and can desync from it
issues.detail: audio_format is computed once as f"pcm_{sample_rate}" then stored alongside sample_rate. Two fields, one fact. If a caller mutates one, the other lies. Drop audio_format from STTOptions and format it at the single use site in _connect_ws. Data dominates: one source of truth makes the bug impossible.

issues.description: STTOptions has eleven Optional fields converted via repeated is_given ternaries; the construction is mostly bookkeeping
issues.detail: The __init__ does the same NotGivenOr-to-None dance for five VAD parameters. This is data shape fighting the code. A small helper (def _coalesce(v): return v if is_given(v) else None) or building the dict and passing **kwargs would reduce ten lines to two and make the parameter set obvious. Small composable transform over data.

issues.description: _connect_ws builds the query string by hand instead of letting aiohttp do it
issues.detail: Manual list-of-f-strings joined with '&' reinvents URL encoding. aiohttp.ClientSession.ws_connect accepts a params= dict; building one from {k: v for k, v in candidates.items() if v is not None} is shorter, safer if any value ever contains a special char, and obvious. The language should help you not write code.

issues.description: The receive-side dispatch is a chain of elif on message_type; a small dict of handlers would make the protocol obvious
issues.detail: _process_stream_event is a flat switch with three near-duplicate branches that all do the same speaking-state bookkeeping. Lift the speaking-state transitions into one helper, and let each message_type be a small function. The data (message kind plus text) drives the algorithm; right now the algorithm is fighting it.

issues.description: STTv2 duplicates ~95% of STT's surface; the v1/v2 split is a copy rather than a composition
issues.detail: Following the Deepgram pattern is fine, but the author notes this is for backward compatibility. The shared parts (auth, session, base URL, capability declaration) should live in one place; v1 and v2 should differ only in the wire protocol. A small base or a shared helper module avoids two files drifting apart over time. Composition over duplication.

review.summary: The plugin works and follows the established Deepgram/Cartesia shape, but the design carries more code than the problem requires. The STTOptions dataclass duplicates derivable fields and converts NotGivenOr with eleven near-identical ternaries; both are data-shape problems where a smaller structure would make the code self-evident. The receive-side handler is a switch with duplicated speaking-state bookkeeping that wants to be a small table or helper. Two real concerns: error message types raise inside recv_task's broad except and get swallowed, and the v2 file is a near-copy of v1 with no shared base — fine today, drift tomorrow. Decision: TOO-MUCH-FRAMEWORK and one WRONG-DATA-STRUCTURE; nothing here blocks merge but the data structures should be tightened before the v1/v2 pair calcifies.
